project.name: Warp Keybindings Subsystem
project.description: An accurate, adversarially-verified map of how keyboard shortcuts work in Warp: the keymap engine (Keymap/Matcher/ContextPredicate/overlap conflict oracle), the keystroke→action dispatch + responder chain, the keybindings.yaml config + load/override/persist path, the settings-UI editor + cheatsheet, and the modal (vim) editing pipeline (pure FSA → VimEvent → VimHandler) with its reusable buffer algorithms. Scoped to the keybinding-relevant code across the warpui_core, vim, and editor crates plus the warp app integration layer.

nodes.name: vim_handler.rs
nodes.summary: Code-editor implementation of the vim `VimHandler` trait: lowers FSA-produced vim events into concrete buffer mutations and motions (operations, visual operators, paste, join, search, scroll) for the rich-text code editor.

nodes.name: element.rs
nodes.summary: GPUI element for the input/code editor; keybinding-relevant parts are the printable-character input fork (`typed_characters`) that routes to VimUserInsert vs UserInsert based on vim mode, and cursor-shape-by-mode selection.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Terminal/input editor view; hosts keybinding registration (`init`), the keymap context predicate, the `EditorAction` taxonomy, and the terminal editor's `VimHandler` impl plus the vim keystroke/insert plumbing.

nodes.name: find_char.rs
nodes.summary: Pure helper computing the target column for vim find-char motions (f/F/t/T) within a single line, honoring occurrence count and selection state.

nodes.name: matching_brackets.rs
nodes.summary: Pure helper that locates the matching bracket for a bracket character at a buffer offset, used by the vim `%` matching-bracket motion.

nodes.name: register.rs
nodes.summary: Tiny helper validating vim register names (a–z, 0–9, and special registers).

nodes.name: block.rs
nodes.summary: Vim block text-object algorithms (`ib`/`ab`, parens/brackets/braces): finds the inner and around ranges for bracket-delimited blocks at a buffer offset.

nodes.name: vim_find_char_on_line
nodes.summary: Computes the destination column for a vim find-char motion (f/F/t/T) on one line, applying occurrence count, till-offset, and selection preservation.

nodes.name: vim_find_matching_bracket
nodes.summary: Scans outward from an offset to find the matching partner of a bracket character, used by the vim `%` motion.

nodes.name: valid_register_name
nodes.summary: Returns whether a character is a valid vim register name.

nodes.name: vim_inner_block
nodes.summary: Computes the inner range of a bracket-delimited block (`ib`) at an offset, optionally preserving leading padding.

nodes.name: vim_a_block
nodes.summary: Computes the around range of a bracket-delimited block (`ab`), including the surrounding brackets.

nodes.name: operation
nodes.summary: Applies a vim operator+operand operation (delete/change/yank over a motion or text object) to the code buffer, the central operator-execution dispatch of the handler.

nodes.name: navigate_char
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor by a character motion, honoring counts, line bounds, and vim normal-mode column clamping.

nodes.name: navigate_word
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor by a word motion (w/b/e/W/B/E) using the vim word iterator.

nodes.name: navigate_line
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor by a line motion (j/k/0/$/G), adjusting target column appropriately.

nodes.name: first_nonwhitespace_motion
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor to the first non-whitespace character of the target line (`^`).

nodes.name: find_char
nodes.summary: Executes a find-char motion (f/F/t/T) by delegating to the vim find-char column computation.

nodes.name: navigate_paragraph
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor by paragraph ({/}) in the code buffer.

nodes.name: visual_operator
nodes.summary: Applies an operator to the current visual selection (delete/change/yank/case) in the code editor.

nodes.name: visual_paste
nodes.summary: Pastes register contents over the active visual selection, replacing it.

nodes.name: paste
nodes.summary: Pastes register contents at the cursor with vim characterwise/linewise semantics and cursor placement.

nodes.name: join_line
nodes.summary: Joins the current line with the next (J/gJ), collapsing whitespace per vim rules.

nodes.name: change_mode
nodes.summary: Applies a vim mode transition in the code editor, adjusting selection and cursor shape for the new mode.

nodes.name: cycle_search
nodes.summary: Cycles to the next/previous search match (n/N) in the code editor.

nodes.name: search_word_at_cursor
nodes.summary: Starts a search for the word under the cursor (* / #).

nodes.name: scroll_half_page
nodes.summary: Scrolls the viewport a half page (Ctrl-D/Ctrl-U) and repositions the cursor.

nodes.name: typed_characters
nodes.summary: The printable-character input fork: when a vim mode is active dispatches `EditorAction::VimUserInsert`, otherwise `EditorAction::UserInsert`, routing keystrokes into either the FSA or plain insertion.

nodes.name: get_cursor_type
nodes.summary: Selects the cursor display shape from the active vim mode (Block for Normal/Visual, Underline for Replace, Bar for Insert).

nodes.name: EditorAction
nodes.summary: Enum of all editor actions bound to keystrokes, including the vim fork actions `VimUserInsert`/`UserInsert` and `VimBackspace`/`VimEscape` plus standard editing commands.

nodes.name: EditorView
nodes.summary: The terminal/input editor view; holds the `VimModel` and `supports_vim_mode` flag and is the `EditorView` target of the terminal editor's `VimHandler` impl.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Registers all editor keybindings via `register_fixed_bindings`/`register_editable_bindings`, wiring keystrokes (including VimBackspace/VimEscape) to `EditorAction`s.

nodes.name: keymap_context
nodes.summary: Builds the keymap context predicate for the editor (including vim-mode contexts) used to scope which bindings are active.

nodes.name: handle_action
nodes.summary: Central action dispatcher mapping a resolved `EditorAction` (including the vim insert/backspace/escape forks) to editor behavior.

nodes.name: operation
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` operator-execution: applies a vim operator+operand to the input buffer.

nodes.name: navigate_char
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` character motion with vim column-clamping and propagation rules.

nodes.name: join_line
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` line-join (J) implementation.

nodes.name: visual_operator
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` visual-mode operator application.

nodes.name: visual_text_object
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` visual-mode text-object selection (e.g. viw, ci").

nodes.name: change_mode
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` mode transition, updating selection/cursor on Normal/Insert/Visual changes.

nodes.name: insert_text
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` text insertion path used when applying vim insert events.

nodes.name: visual_paste
nodes.summary: Terminal editor's `VimHandler` paste over a visual selection.

nodes.name: vim_keystroke
nodes.summary: Feeds a full keystroke into the editor's `VimModel`, advancing the FSA and emitting vim events for the handler.

nodes.name: vim_user_insert
nodes.summary: Handles `VimUserInsert`: forwards typed characters into the `VimModel` so insert-mode text and FSA commands are processed.

nodes.name: vim_apply_insert_position
nodes.summary: Positions the cursor when entering insert mode (i/a/I/A/o/O) according to the requested `InsertPosition`.

nodes.name: vim_cursor_forward_word
nodes.summary: Moves the cursor forward by a word for vim word motions, applying word/WORD boundary semantics in the terminal editor.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Barrel module for the vim text-objects submodule, re-exporting block/quote/word text-object helpers.

nodes.name: quote.rs
nodes.summary: Vim quote text-object algorithms (`i"`/`a"`, single/double/backtick): computes inner and around ranges for quote-delimited text at a buffer offset.

nodes.name: quote_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests exercising the vim quote text-object inner/around range computations.

nodes.name: word.rs
nodes.summary: Vim word text-object algorithms (`iw`/`aw`, word vs WORD): computes inner and around word ranges using the shared word iterator.

nodes.name: vim.rs
nodes.summary: Core vim engine: the pure `VimFSA` finite-state automaton that turns keystrokes/typed characters into `VimEvent`s across normal/visual/insert/replace modes, plus the `VimHandler` trait, `VimModel` public API, and the full motion/operator/text-object type taxonomy.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure FSA design: VimFSA holds no buffer; it emits VimEvent values that a VimHandler implementor applies, keeping keystroke parsing testable and host-agnostic.

nodes.name: word_iterator.rs
nodes.summary: Bidirectional word iterator over a buffer used by vim word motions and word text-objects; classifies characters into word/symbol/whitespace kinds and yields word head/tail offsets.

nodes.name: VimFSA
nodes.summary: The pure vim finite-state automaton: tracks mode and pending operator/operand/count and turns each keystroke or typed character into lowered `VimEvent`s without touching any buffer.

nodes.name: VimMode
nodes.summary: Enum of vim editor modes (Normal, Insert, Visual(motion), Replace) that drives input forking and cursor shape.

nodes.name: VimHandler
nodes.summary: Trait defining every action the FSA can request of a host editor (insert, motions, operations, visual operators, paste, search, jumps, scroll); implemented per editor to apply vim events to a real buffer.

nodes.name: VimModel
nodes.summary: Public stateful wrapper around `VimFSA` exposing `typed_character`/`keypress`/`force_insert_mode`/`interrupt` as the editor-facing vim API.

nodes.name: VimSubscriber
nodes.summary: Trait whose default `handle_vim_event` lowers a `VimEvent` into the appropriate `VimHandler` method call, bridging FSA output to editor actions.

nodes.name: VimEvent
nodes.summary: A single lowered vim command (event type plus count) emitted by the FSA for the handler to execute.

nodes.name: VimEventType
nodes.summary: Exhaustive taxonomy of vim commands the FSA can emit (motions, operations, mode changes, paste, search, jumps, scroll, dot-repeat).

nodes.name: VimMotion
nodes.summary: Enum of vim cursor motions (char/word/line/paragraph/find-char/first-non-whitespace/bracket) produced from keystrokes.

nodes.name: VimTextObject
nodes.summary: Represents a vim text object (inner/around word, quote, or block) targeted by operators in normal and visual modes.

nodes.name: VimOperator
nodes.summary: Enum of vim operators (delete, change, yank, etc.) that combine with a motion or text object to form an operation.

nodes.name: VimOperand
nodes.summary: The operand (motion or text object) an operator acts on when forming a complete vim operation.

nodes.name: typed_character
nodes.summary: FSA entry for a printable character: routes to the mode-specific normal/visual/insert handlers and returns any resulting `VimEvent`s.

nodes.name: keypress
nodes.summary: FSA entry for a full keystroke (with modifiers/special keys): maps Escape/Backspace/Delete/Enter and modified chords to mode transitions or events before falling through to typed-character handling.

nodes.name: compute_event_count
nodes.summary: Computes the repetition count for an event by multiplying any pending operator count with the motion/operand count.

nodes.name: exit_insert_mode
nodes.summary: Handles leaving insert mode: finalizes dot-repeat text and emits the mode-transition event back to normal mode.

nodes.name: handle_normal_nothing_pending
nodes.summary: Core normal-mode dispatch with no pending operator: maps a typed character to a motion, operator, mode change, paste, jump, or immediate command.

nodes.name: handle_normal_pending_action
nodes.summary: Resolves a normal-mode keystroke when an action (e.g. find-char, replace, register) is pending its argument character.

nodes.name: handle_normal_pending_operation
nodes.summary: Resolves the second key of an operator-pending sequence (e.g. `d`+motion, `c`+text-object) into a complete operation event.

nodes.name: handle_normal_pending_operand
nodes.summary: Completes an operator+text-object pairing (e.g. `di(`, `ciw`) once the operand's final character arrives.

nodes.name: handle_visual_command
nodes.summary: Builds a visual-mode operation event from the current visual selection and an operator keystroke.

nodes.name: handle_visual_nothing_pending
nodes.summary: Visual-mode dispatch with nothing pending: maps a keystroke to a selection-extending motion, operator, text object, or mode change.

nodes.name: handle_visual_pending_action
nodes.summary: Resolves a visual-mode keystroke awaiting an argument (find-char target, text-object qualifier).

nodes.name: create_visual_operator
nodes.summary: Constructs a visual-mode operator event from the active selection range and the chosen operator.

nodes.name: for_dot_repeat
nodes.summary: Determines whether and how a `VimEventType` is recorded for dot (`.`) repeat, returning the repeatable event variant.

nodes.name: try_from
nodes.summary: Parses a character into a `BracketChar`, classifying open/close parens, brackets, and braces for bracket motions and block text objects.

nodes.name: handle_vim_event
nodes.summary: Default `VimSubscriber` implementation that pattern-matches a `VimEvent` and invokes the matching `VimHandler` method, lowering FSA output into editor actions.

nodes.name: word_motion_for_character
nodes.summary: Maps a word-motion keystroke (w/b/e/W/B/E) to the corresponding `WordMotion` descriptor.

nodes.name: char_motion_for_character
nodes.summary: Maps a character-motion keystroke (h/l/space/backspace) to a `CharacterMotion`.

nodes.name: closed_word_motion_for_character
nodes.summary: Maps a keystroke to a word motion for operator-pending contexts where end-inclusive semantics differ.

nodes.name: CharacterKind
nodes.summary: Classification of a character as word-char, symbol, or whitespace, the basis for vim word-boundary detection.

nodes.name: WordHeadsVim
nodes.summary: Iterator yielding successive word-head offsets in a direction, powering vim w/b word motions and word text objects.

nodes.name: WordTailsVim
nodes.summary: Iterator yielding successive word-tail (end-of-word) offsets, powering vim e/ge motions.

nodes.name: vim_word_iterator_from_offset
nodes.summary: Factory returning the appropriate word-head/tail iterator for a starting offset, direction, bound, and word type.

nodes.name: equivalent_char_kind
nodes.summary: Decides whether two characters belong to the same vim word group (word vs WORD semantics), defining word boundaries.

nodes.name: vim_inner_quote
nodes.summary: Computes the inner range of quote-delimited text (`i"`) at an offset.

nodes.name: vim_a_quote
nodes.summary: Computes the around range of quote-delimited text (`a"`), including the quotes and trailing whitespace per vim rules.

nodes.name: vim_inner_word
nodes.summary: Computes the inner word range (`iw`) at an offset using the shared word iterator and word/WORD semantics.

nodes.name: vim_a_word
nodes.summary: Computes the around word range (`aw`), extending over trailing or leading whitespace per vim rules.

nodes.name: keyboard.rs
nodes.summary: Reads, writes, and loads the user's keybindings.yaml file, converting persisted normalized keystroke strings into runtime custom triggers applied to the app keymap.
nodes.languageNotes: cfg-gated: real fs-backed impls on desktop, no-op stubs on other targets (note the duplicate fn names under cfg attributes).

nodes.name: keymap_resolution_snapshot_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Golden snapshot test that resolves a fixed keystroke/context matrix against the keymap and diffs the formatted winning bindings against a checked-in expectation file.

nodes.name: keybindings_page.rs
nodes.summary: Resource-center cheatsheet page that groups all command bindings into sections, renders them as a searchable keyboard-shortcut reference, and reacts to live keybinding changes.

nodes.name: utils.rs
nodes.summary: Helper utilities for the resource center, including assembling the supplemental catalog of additional keybindings shown alongside the editable command bindings.

nodes.name: root_view.rs
nodes.summary: Top-level application view that owns window lifecycle, onboarding/auth, and quake mode; for keybindings it registers the root fixed/editable bindings during init and supplies the root keymap context and action dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large multi-purpose view; only binding-registration and keymap wiring symbols extracted for the keybindings graph.

nodes.name: keybindings.rs
nodes.summary: Settings-UI keybindings editor: lists editable bindings, captures a new keystroke per row, detects conflicts via a ConflictMap, and confirms/resets/removes custom triggers.

nodes.name: UserDefinedKeybinding
nodes.summary: Enum representing a user-defined keybinding parsed from keybindings.yaml — either a list of keystrokes or an explicit removal (tombstone).

nodes.name: load_custom_keybindings
nodes.summary: Reads the user keybindings file and applies each entry to the app as a custom trigger (or removes it), the entry point for honoring user keymap overrides at startup.

nodes.name: write_custom_keybinding
nodes.summary: Persists a single custom keybinding (name + keystrokes) into the user's keybindings map on disk.

nodes.name: remove_custom_keybinding
nodes.summary: Removes/overrides a keybinding in the persisted map, recording a tombstone so a default binding stays disabled.

nodes.name: save_custom_keybindings
nodes.summary: Serializes the full custom keybindings map to YAML and atomically writes it to the keybinding file path.

nodes.name: read_custom_keybindings
nodes.summary: Loads and deserializes the persisted custom keybindings map from disk, returning an empty map when absent.

nodes.name: try_from
nodes.summary: Parses a PersistedTrigger's normalized string into a Vec of validated Keystrokes, erroring on any unparseable keystroke.

nodes.name: x13_resolution_snapshot
nodes.summary: The golden test: resolves every keystroke against a built context set, formats the winning binding per cell, and diffs the table against the checked-in snapshot.

nodes.name: build_context
nodes.summary: Constructs the keymap Context (view id, predicates) used as input for the resolution snapshot matrix.

nodes.name: fmt_keystroke
nodes.summary: Formats a Keystroke into a stable display string for inclusion in the golden snapshot output.

nodes.name: print_diff
nodes.summary: Renders a human-readable diff between expected and actual snapshot tables when the golden assertion fails.

nodes.name: KeybindingsView
nodes.summary: Resource-center cheatsheet view holding the grouped binding rows, search bar/editor and scroll state for the keyboard-shortcut reference page.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Builds the cheatsheet view: wires the search editor, subscribes to keybinding-change notifications, and assembles the initial sectioned binding list.

nodes.name: build_bindings
nodes.summary: Collects all command bindings, partitions them into sections, and produces the displayable cheatsheet content.

nodes.name: rebuild_bindings
nodes.summary: Re-filters the bindings against the current search query and refreshes the rendered binding list.

nodes.name: handle_keybinding_changed
nodes.summary: Reacts to a live keybinding change event by updating the affected rows' displayed triggers in place.

nodes.name: handle_search_editor_event
nodes.summary: Handles search-editor input events, re-running the keystroke-aware filter and updating results.

nodes.name: get_bindings_by_section
nodes.summary: Maps a KeybindingSection enum to the concrete set of command bindings (essentials, blocks, input editor, terminal, fundamentals) shown under it.

nodes.name: update_binding_with_new_trigger
nodes.summary: Updates a binding row in the local list with a newly assigned trigger, returning whether a visible row changed.

nodes.name: get_additional_keybindings
nodes.summary: Assembles the static catalog of supplemental (non-editable) keybindings displayed in the resource center alongside the editable command bindings.

nodes.name: RootViewAction
nodes.summary: Action enum for the root view (toggle quake mode, show/hide windows, toggle fullscreen, debug onboarding) dispatched through the keymap.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Root view initializer that registers the application-level fixed and editable key bindings (register_fixed_bindings / register_editable_bindings) plus global window shortcuts.

nodes.name: maybe_register_global_window_shortcuts
nodes.summary: Registers OS-level global window shortcuts (e.g. quake-mode toggle) when enabled by settings.

nodes.name: keymap_context
nodes.summary: Produces the root view's keymap context (predicates/identifiers) used as the base for resolving keyboard shortcuts in the responder tree.

nodes.name: handle_action
nodes.summary: Dispatches a resolved RootViewAction to the corresponding root-view behavior (quake mode, fullscreen, etc.).

nodes.name: ConflictMap
nodes.summary: Tracks which keystrokes are bound by more than one enabled binding, enabling conflict highlighting in the settings editor.

nodes.name: KeyBindingModifyingState
nodes.summary: Per-row capture state holding the current binding and the unsaved keystroke being edited, with dirty tracking.

nodes.name: KeybindingsView
nodes.summary: Settings page view listing editable bindings with search, per-row modifying state, rendered rows and a live conflict map.

nodes.name: KeybindingsViewAction
nodes.summary: Action enum for the settings keybindings editor (row clicked, keystroke defined, reset/cancel/confirm/remove).

nodes.name: KeybindingRow
nodes.summary: Render model for a single editable binding row, including its mouse states and open/closed editor flag.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Updates the conflict map when a binding's keystroke changes, decrementing the old key and incrementing the new one.

nodes.name: has_conflict
nodes.summary: Returns whether a given keystroke is currently bound by more than one enabled binding.

nodes.name: from_iter
nodes.summary: Builds a ConflictMap by counting keystroke occurrences across an iterator of bindings.

nodes.name: confirm_keystroke_editing
nodes.summary: Confirms the captured keystroke for a row, applying it as a custom keybinding and refreshing conflicts.

nodes.name: set_temporary_keystroke_state
nodes.summary: Stores the in-progress captured keystroke for a row while the user is recording a new shortcut.

nodes.name: binding_row_clicked
nodes.summary: Opens a row for editing, entering keystroke-capture mode for that binding.

nodes.name: remove_keystroke
nodes.summary: Removes the binding's keystroke by setting an empty custom trigger (tombstone) and updating the conflict map.

nodes.name: reset_to_default_keystroke
nodes.summary: Resets a binding back to its default trigger via reset_keybinding_to_default and refreshes the row.

nodes.name: cancel_keystroke_editing
nodes.summary: Cancels an in-progress keystroke capture, discarding the unsaved binding and closing the row editor.

nodes.name: filter_bindings
nodes.summary: Filters the editable binding list against the search query using the shared keystroke-aware filter.

nodes.name: handle_search_editor_event
nodes.summary: Handles search-editor events in the settings page, re-applying the binding filter.

nodes.name: on_page_selected
nodes.summary: Initializes the keybindings settings page when selected: builds binding rows, the conflict map, and focus state.

nodes.name: handle_action
nodes.summary: Dispatches a KeybindingsViewAction (row clicked, confirm, reset, cancel, remove) to the matching editor handler.

nodes.name: trigger_keybinding_notifier
nodes.summary: Emits a keybinding-changed notification so other views (e.g. the cheatsheet) update their displayed triggers.

nodes.name: update_binding_list
nodes.summary: Updates the in-memory binding list with a new trigger for the named binding.

nodes.name: init.rs
nodes.summary: Initializes the terminal view, registering the bulk of the terminal's fixed and per-platform key bindings (navigation, paste, input-mode and overlapping bindings) and wiring StandardAction shortcuts.
nodes.languageNotes: Only binding-registration and StandardAction wiring extracted; the rest of terminal init is out of keybindings scope.

nodes.name: bindings.rs
nodes.summary: Bridge layer between the warpui keymap and the app: defines the CustomAction catalog, maps actions to default keystrokes, builds CommandBinding rows, and provides keystroke-aware search/filter plus set/reset of custom keybindings.

nodes.name: keyboard_protocol.rs
nodes.summary: Integration tests for the terminal keyboard protocol (Kitty-style), verifying shift-enter, shifted-symbol unshifted keycodes, alternate keys, query/apply modes, event types, and modifier reporting.

nodes.name: keymap.rs
nodes.summary: Core keymap subsystem: defines Keystroke parsing/normalization, Trigger kinds, FixedBinding/EditableBinding, the layered Keymap/LayerStore (default/user/modepack) and binding descriptions that drive all keyboard-shortcut resolution.
nodes.languageNotes: Layered keymap with default/user/modepack layers; EditableBinding builder pattern and per-platform keystrokes via PerPlatformKeystroke.

nodes.name: matcher_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for keymap matching: keystroke/standard/custom resolution, context-predicate filtering, editable binding matching, and tombstone suppression of inherited bindings.

nodes.name: overlap_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Property/differential tests for context-predicate overlap detection, checking the can-both-be-true satisfiability logic against a brute-force oracle plus adversarial unsat/sat cases.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Massive terminal-view initializer that registers nearly all terminal fixed/per-platform key bindings (navigation, paste, scrolling) and wires StandardAction shortcuts via register_fixed_bindings.

nodes.name: init_overlapping_keybindings
nodes.summary: Registers the terminal's overlapping keybindings that intentionally share keystrokes resolved by context predicates.

nodes.name: register_input_mode_bindings
nodes.summary: Registers the terminal input-mode specific key bindings, gating them by the active input/IME context.

nodes.name: CustomAction
nodes.summary: Exhaustive enum of every user-bindable app command (new tab, copy, paste, splits, palettes, drive actions, etc.) — the catalog that editable keybindings target.

nodes.name: CommandBinding
nodes.summary: UI-facing binding row bridging a keymap binding to a display name, description, trigger, action and group; built from fixed or editable binding lenses.

nodes.name: BindingGroup
nodes.summary: Enum categorizing bindings into display groups (settings, navigation, workflows, terminal, etc.) with string conversions.

nodes.name: trigger_to_keystroke
nodes.summary: Resolves a Trigger (standard/custom/keystrokes) into the concrete default Keystroke used for display and search.

nodes.name: set_custom_keybinding

nodes.summary: Clears a binding's custom trigger, restoring (and persisting) its default keystroke.

nodes.name: convert_search_term_to_keystroke
nodes.summary: Parses a user search term into a (partial) Keystroke so the cheatsheet/settings search can match by key combination.

nodes.name: filter_bindings_including_keystroke
nodes.summary: Filters and scores command bindings against a search term, matching both descriptive text and keystroke similarity.

nodes.name: keystroke_includes
nodes.summary: Predicate testing whether a candidate keystroke contains/matches a (possibly partial) search keystroke.

nodes.name: is_binding_pty_compliant
nodes.summary: Determines whether a binding's keystroke is safe to forward to the PTY (not reserved by terminal input handling).

nodes.name: is_binding_cross_platform

nodes.name: cmd_or_ctrl_shift

nodes.summary: Verifies shift-enter behavior when the keyboard protocol is disabled (legacy CR/newline encoding).

nodes.name: test_keyboard_protocol_enabled_shift_enter
nodes.summary: Verifies shift-enter emits the protocol-encoded sequence when the keyboard protocol is enabled.

nodes.name: test_keyboard_protocol_enabled_shifted_symbol_uses_unshifted_keycode
nodes.summary: Asserts shifted symbols report the unshifted base keycode plus a shift modifier under the protocol.

nodes.name: test_keyboard_protocol_alternate_keys_and_text

nodes.name: test_keyboard_protocol_query_and_apply_modes

nodes.name: test_keyboard_protocol_report_all_keys_printable_and_cursor

nodes.name: test_keyboard_protocol_modifier_key_reporting

nodes.name: test_keyboard_protocol_modifier_self_bit

nodes.name: LayerStore
nodes.summary: Holds the fixed and editable bindings for a single keymap layer, indexed by name, with registration and lookup helpers.

nodes.name: Keymap
nodes.summary: The layered keymap (default/user/modepack) that registers bindings, resolves them high-to-low, and exposes editable/custom-action binding queries.

nodes.name: Trigger
nodes.summary: Enum of binding trigger kinds: explicit keystrokes, a StandardAction reference, a CustomAction reference, or Empty (tombstone).

nodes.name: BindingDescription
nodes.summary: Describes a binding's human-readable label with optional per-context custom text and a dynamic override resolver.

nodes.name: FixedBinding
nodes.summary: A non-editable binding mapping a (per-platform) keystroke/standard/custom trigger to an action under a context predicate.

nodes.name: EditableBinding
nodes.summary: A user-editable binding built via a fluent builder, carrying a name, default and custom triggers, context predicate and tombstone flag.

nodes.name: Keystroke
nodes.summary: Core keystroke value (ctrl/alt/shift/cmd/meta + key) with parsing, normalization, display, validation and JSON-schema/file serialization.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses a keystroke string (e.g. 'cmd-shift-R', 'cmdorctrl-x') into a Keystroke, validating modifiers and key names.

nodes.name: normalized
nodes.summary: Produces the canonical normalized string for a keystroke (stable modifier order/casing) used for persistence and comparison.

nodes.name: displayed
nodes.summary: Renders a keystroke as a human-facing display string with platform-appropriate symbols.

nodes.name: materialized
nodes.summary: Resolves a BindingDescription against a context into a concrete display string, applying custom and dynamic overrides.

nodes.name: register_fixed_bindings
nodes.summary: Registers a batch of FixedBindings into the keymap's default layer.

nodes.name: register_editable_bindings
nodes.summary: Registers a batch of EditableBindings (user-overridable) into the keymap.

nodes.name: test_matcher
nodes.summary: Core matcher test covering keystroke resolution against fixed bindings and context predicates.

nodes.name: test_editable_binding_matching
nodes.summary: Tests that editable bindings (with custom triggers) resolve correctly against keystrokes and contexts.

nodes.name: test_bindings_for_context
nodes.summary: Verifies the set of bindings returned for a given context snapshot is complete and correctly filtered.

nodes.name: test_tombstone_suppresses_keystroke_via_shared_helper
nodes.summary: Asserts an empty/tombstone trigger suppresses an inherited keystroke binding.

nodes.name: test_tombstone_suppresses_standard_via_shared_helper
nodes.summary: Asserts a tombstone suppresses an inherited StandardAction binding.

nodes.name: test_tombstone_suppresses_custom_primary_and_second_surface
nodes.summary: Asserts a tombstone suppresses a CustomAction binding on both its primary and secondary surfaces.

nodes.name: test_tombstone_suppresses_custom_via_original_trigger_dual_check
nodes.summary: Asserts custom-action tombstoning is checked against the original trigger via a dual-check path.

nodes.name: test_inject_override_consistency_gate
nodes.summary: Validates the consistency gate that governs injecting an override binding over an existing one.

nodes.name: oracle_can_both
nodes.summary: Brute-force oracle that decides whether two context predicates can both be true by enumerating atom assignments.

nodes.name: random_predicate
nodes.summary: Generates a random nested context predicate of bounded depth for property testing.

nodes.name: differential_can_both_be_true_matches_brute_force_oracle
nodes.summary: Property test asserting the production can-both-be-true overlap check agrees with the brute-force oracle across random predicates.

nodes.name: guard_returns_conservative_true_and_counts_overflow
nodes.summary: Verifies the overlap guard returns a conservative true and counts overflow when the atom set is too large.

nodes.name: actions.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the StandardAction enum of OS-level standard actions (close, hide, quit, paste, fullscreen, etc.) that serve as built-in keybinding triggers.

nodes.name: app.rs
nodes.summary: Core App/AppContext implementation that owns the keystroke matcher and drives the full keystroke / standard / custom action dispatch down the responder chain, plus binding registration, custom-trigger overrides, and the typed-action handler registry.
nodes.languageNotes: The responder chain is iterated in reverse (bottom-up) so the view closest to focus wins; matcher results are an enum (None/Pending/Action/Unbound) where Unbound is a tombstone suppression.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Core framework module defining shared entity/view primitives, including the type-erased AnyView trait whose keymap_context hook yields each view's keybinding Context.

nodes.name: context.rs
nodes.summary: Defines ViewContext, the per-view dispatch surface that exposes typed/global action dispatch and the key-binding enable/disable controls used while editing keybindings.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the View and TypedActionView traits, including keymap_context / default_keymap_context that construct each view's keybinding context from its ui_name.

nodes.name: matcher.rs
nodes.summary: The keystroke matching kernel (Matcher): registers fixed/editable bindings, applies custom-trigger overrides, accumulates chord keystrokes per view, and resolves keystroke/standard/custom triggers to actions within a Context.
nodes.languageNotes: MatchResult enum (None/Pending/Action/Unbound) drives dispatch; tombstone bindings resolve to Unbound to suppress lower-precedence bindings on the same key.

nodes.name: StandardAction
nodes.summary: Enum of OS-level standard actions (Close, Hide, Quit, Zoom, Minimize, ToggleFullScreen, Paste, etc.) used as a Trigger variant in the keymap.

nodes.name: Matcher
nodes.summary: The keystroke matching engine wrapping a Keymap; holds per-view pending chord state and binding validators, and exposes registration, custom-trigger override, validation, and push/match resolution.

nodes.name: Pending
nodes.summary: Per-view chord-in-progress state holding the accumulated keystrokes and the Context they were matched against, used to resolve multi-keystroke bindings.

nodes.name: IsBindingValid
nodes.summary: Yes/No result returned by binding validators to signal whether a registered binding passes validation.

nodes.name: MatchResult
nodes.summary: Outcome of a keystroke/standard/custom match attempt: None, Pending (partial chord), Action (resolved binding), or Unbound (tombstone suppression).

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Public application handle exposing keybinding entry points (dispatch_action/dispatch_typed_action/dispatch_keystroke, register bindings, set custom triggers) that delegate to the underlying AppContext.

nodes.name: AppContext
nodes.summary: The mutable application context that owns the keystroke_matcher, the typed-action handler registry, window/view state, and implements the responder-chain dispatch and binding-management logic.

nodes.name: AnyView
nodes.summary: Type-erased view trait used by the framework; its keymap_context method produces the view's keybinding Context that dispatch merges up the responder chain.

nodes.name: ViewContext
nodes.summary: Per-view context passed to view handlers, exposing action dispatch (typed/global/deferred), key-binding enable/disable controls, and view/model lifecycle helpers.

nodes.name: View
nodes.summary: The core typed view trait; defines keymap_context and default_keymap_context that build the keybinding Context for a view (defaulting to a context containing the view's ui_name).

nodes.name: TypedActionView
nodes.summary: Trait for views that handle a specific typed Action; handle_action is the registered entry point invoked when a matched action is dispatched to the view.

nodes.name: push_keystroke
nodes.summary: Chord-aware keystroke matcher: accumulates pending keystrokes per view (clearing them on context change), then matches the prefix against keystroke-trigger bindings whose context predicate holds, returning Action, Pending, Unbound, or None.

nodes.name: match_standard
nodes.summary: Matches a StandardAction against bindings with a matching Standard trigger whose context predicate holds, returning the resolved action (never Pending).

nodes.name: match_custom
nodes.summary: Matches a custom action tag against bindings, checking both the current Custom trigger and any original (overridden) Custom trigger, returning the resolved action in context.

nodes.name: resolve_matched_binding
nodes.summary: Shared helper turning a matched binding lens into a MatchResult: tombstone bindings become Unbound (suppression), otherwise the binding's action wins.

nodes.name: register_fixed_bindings
nodes.summary: Registers fixed (non-editable) bindings into the keymap, converting any custom triggers to keystroke triggers via the configured fn and clearing pending chord state.

nodes.name: register_editable_bindings
nodes.summary: Registers named editable bindings (overridable via set_custom_trigger), converting custom triggers to keystroke triggers and clearing pending state.

nodes.name: set_custom_trigger
nodes.summary: Overrides the default trigger of a named editable binding with a user-supplied trigger and clears pending chord state.

nodes.name: validate_bindings
nodes.summary: Debug-only pass running each registered context validator plus the default validator over all matching bindings, panicking if any binding is invalid.

nodes.name: binding_for_custom_action_in_context
nodes.summary: Resolves the active binding for a custom action tag honoring the supplied contexts and context predicates, used for menu/keystroke lookups.

nodes.name: dispatch_keystroke
nodes.summary: Core keystroke dispatch: builds a Context per responder-chain link, injects IMEOpen when composing, pushes the keystroke into the matcher bottom-up, and dispatches the resulting typed action; tracks pending chords.

nodes.name: dispatch_typed_action
nodes.summary: Looks up the registered handler for an action's type and the target view's type in the typed_actions registry and invokes it on the view, walking up the responder chain.

nodes.name: dispatch_standard_action
nodes.summary: Matches a StandardAction across the responder chain (bottom-up) and dispatches the resolved typed action, with special interaction handling for Paste.

nodes.name: dispatch_custom_action
nodes.summary: Public custom-action dispatch entry: dispatches via the responder chain when key bindings are enabled, otherwise falls back to keystroke synthesis while the user is editing keybindings.

nodes.name: dispatch_custom_action_internal
nodes.summary: Matches a custom action tag against the matcher for each responder-chain context (bottom-up) and dispatches the resolved typed action.

nodes.name: dispatch_custom_action_keystroke
nodes.summary: Resolves the keystroke currently bound to a custom action and dispatches it as a raw key event; used when editing keybindings so a menu-bound action can be re-handled as a keystroke.

nodes.name: add_typed_action
nodes.summary: Registers a typed action handler into the typed_actions registry keyed by (ActionType, ViewType); the boxed handler downcasts and invokes the view's TypedActionView::handle_action plus a11y reporting.

nodes.name: key_bindings_for_view
nodes.summary: Collects the bindings that apply to a window/view in precedence order (responder contexts reversed bottom-up), keeping only the first binding per trigger so it reflects what would actually fire.

nodes.name: editable_bindings_for_view
nodes.summary: Returns all editable bindings applicable in a window/view's responder-chain contexts, regardless of whether they currently have a key binding (used by the keybindings settings UI).

nodes.name: contexts_from_responder_chain
nodes.summary: Builds a Context for each view in a responder chain via view.keymap_context, injecting IMEOpen when the platform IME is open; errors if a view is missing.

nodes.name: contexts_for_window_and_view
nodes.summary: Resolves the responder chain ancestors for a view and maps them to their keymap contexts, returning an empty list on error.

nodes.name: register_fixed_bindings
nodes.summary: App-level entry point that registers fixed bindings into the keystroke matcher.

nodes.name: register_editable_bindings
nodes.summary: App-level entry point registering named editable bindings (overridable via set_custom_trigger) into the keystroke matcher.

nodes.name: set_custom_trigger
nodes.summary: App-level entry point overriding the default trigger of a named editable binding with a custom trigger.

nodes.name: remove_custom_trigger
nodes.summary: Removes any custom trigger for a named binding, returning it to its default trigger state.

nodes.name: update_custom_action_binding
nodes.summary: Runs an updater callback with the currently active binding for a custom action (in the focused window/view context), used to keep menu state in sync.

nodes.name: binding_for_custom_action
nodes.summary: Resolves the binding for a custom action across a set of contexts by delegating to the matcher's context-aware lookup.

nodes.name: get_responder_chain
nodes.summary: Builds the responder chain for a window: the focused view and its ancestors, or the root view when nothing is focused.

nodes.name: dispatch_self_or_child_interacted_with
nodes.summary: Notifies every view in the responder chain that it (or a child) was interacted with, called after a handled keyboard/interaction event.

nodes.name: disable_key_bindings_dispatching
nodes.summary: Disables key-binding dispatch for the view's window (used while the user edits keybindings so raw keystrokes can be captured).

nodes.name: enable_key_bindings_dispatching
nodes.summary: Re-enables key-binding dispatch for the view's window after it was disabled.

nodes.name: dispatch_global_action
nodes.summary: Dispatches a named global action from the view context, routing it to the app's global action handlers.

nodes.name: dispatch_typed_action
nodes.summary: Dispatches a typed action from the view context up the responder chain to the registered handler.

nodes.name: dispatch_typed_action_deferred
nodes.summary: Schedules a typed action to be dispatched on a later frame rather than synchronously, avoiding reentrancy during the current update.

nodes.name: add_typed_action_view
nodes.summary: Spawns a child view that implements TypedActionView, registering its action handler so dispatched actions of its type reach it.

nodes.name: keymap_context
nodes.summary: AnyView trait method returning the view's keymap Context, the type-erased hook the dispatcher calls to build each responder-chain link's context.

nodes.name: keymap_context
nodes.summary: View trait method returning the current UI keymap Context used to compute valid actions/shortcuts; defaults to default_keymap_context.

nodes.name: default_keymap_context
nodes.summary: Constructs the default keymap Context for a view by inserting the view's ui_name into the context set, the base of context-predicate matching.

nodes.name: view.rs
nodes.summary: CodeEditorView, the syntax-highlighted code editor view. Owns the vim model and wires vim mode into keybinding resolution via keymap_context (Vim/VimNormalMode/VimVisualMode flags) and routes keystrokes/typed chars into the VimFSA.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-purpose 2.4k-line view; only vim mode gating, keymap context flagging, and keystroke/char routing are keybinding-relevant.

nodes.name: CodeEditorView
nodes.summary: Main code editor view struct holding a vim_model and supports_vim_mode flag; exposes vim_mode_enabled gating, keymap_context, and the vim_keystroke/vim_user_insert/user_insert input handlers that CodeEditorViewAction handlers dispatch into.

nodes.name: keymap_context
nodes.summary: Builds the keymap Context for the editor, inserting the 'Vim', 'VimNormalMode', and 'VimVisualMode' context flags based on the current VimMode so that dual-registered bindings resolve correctly. Also sets NON_EDITABLE and FindBarAvailable flags.

nodes.name: vim_mode_enabled
nodes.summary: Gate that returns true only when the editor supports vim mode and the user's AppEditorSettings have vim_mode_enabled; consumed by keymap_context and vim_state to decide whether vim bindings apply.

nodes.name: enter_vim_normal_mode
nodes.summary: Forces the editor into vim normal mode (when vim is enabled) by sending an 'escape' keystroke to the VimFSA via vim_escape.

nodes.name: vim_keystroke
nodes.summary: Routes a non-printable Keystroke into the vim model's keypress FSA when the editor is focused; the sink for VimEnter/VimTab/VimDelete/VimEscape action handlers that re-synthesize keystrokes.

nodes.name: vim_user_insert
nodes.summary: Feeds printable characters one at a time into the vim model's typed_character FSA when focused; the vim-mode counterpart of user_insert, invoked by the VimUserTyped action handler.

nodes.name: user_insert
nodes.summary: Non-vim printable-character insertion path: handles closing-symbol step-over and autocomplete-symbol pairing before delegating to the buffer model's user_insert; the sink for the UserTyped action.

nodes.name: vim_apply_insert_position
nodes.summary: Applies a vim InsertPosition (AfterCursor, LineEnd, LineAbove/Below, etc.) by issuing the corresponding cursor/newline motions on the buffer model when entering insert mode from a vim command.

nodes.name: actions.rs
nodes.summary: Keybinding and action layer for CodeEditorView: registers fixed/editable bindings with dual Vim/non-Vim context predicates (e.g. Enter vs VimEnter), defines the CodeEditorViewAction enum, and routes each action to the appropriate vim or non-vim handler.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses id!("Vim") / !id!("Vim") context-predicate macros to dual-register the same keystroke to vim vs non-vim actions.

nodes.name: CodeEditorViewAction
nodes.summary: Enum of every code-editor action, including the dual UserTyped/VimUserTyped typed-char variants and the Vim-prefixed keystroke variants (VimEnter, VimTab, VimDelete, VimBackspace, VimShiftTab, VimShiftEnter, VimEscape) that re-synthesize keystrokes into the vim FSA.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Registers all CodeEditorView key bindings. Builds CodeEditorView & !IMEOpen context predicates and dual-registers keys against id!("Vim") vs !id!("Vim") so Enter/Tab/Backspace/Delete map to either plain editor actions or their Vim* counterparts that drive the vim model.

nodes.name: handle_action
nodes.summary: Central action dispatcher: routes UserTyped to user_insert and VimUserTyped to vim_user_insert (guarding against the find input), and converts Vim* actions (VimEnter/VimTab/VimDelete/VimEscape/ScrollHalfPage) into synthetic keystrokes sent to vim_keystroke.

nodes.name: user_typed
nodes.summary: RichTextAction impl that wraps printable characters into a CodeEditorViewAction::UserTyped action when the editor is editable; the non-vim branch of the typed-character input fork.

nodes.name: vim_user_typed
nodes.summary: RichTextAction impl that wraps printable characters into a CodeEditorViewAction::VimUserTyped action when editable; the vim branch of the typed-character input fork that handle_typed_characters selects when vim_mode is set.

nodes.name: allowed_in_interaction_state
nodes.summary: Determines whether a given CodeEditorViewAction is permitted in the current InteractionState (Editable/Selectable/Disabled), gating action dispatch before handle_action runs.

nodes.name: allowed_in_selectable_state
nodes.summary: Whitelist of which CodeEditorViewAction variants (including UserTyped/VimUserTyped and the Vim* variants) remain allowed when the editor is only selectable rather than fully editable.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Rich-text editor element rendering and input element. Carries an optional VimMode and forks typed-character handling between vim_user_typed and user_typed; also maps VimMode to cursor display shape (Block/Underline/Bar).
nodes.languageNotes: Generic over view type V via the RichTextAction<V> trait so the same element drives both plain and code editors.

nodes.name: RichTextElement
nodes.summary: The rich-text input element that holds the current vim_mode: Option<VimMode> and parent view weak handle; its handle_typed_characters method uses vim_mode to decide which action factory to call.

nodes.name: RichTextAction
nodes.summary: Trait that view action enums implement to be driven by the rich-text element; declares the dual user_typed and vim_user_typed action factories plus scroll and mouse event constructors.

nodes.name: handle_typed_characters
nodes.summary: The printable-character input fork: when vim_mode is Some it builds an action via vim_user_typed, otherwise via user_typed, then dispatches the resulting typed action to the parent view.

nodes.name: editor.rs
nodes.summary: Editor settings group defining text-editing and appearance preferences, including the `vim_mode` setting (toml path `text_editing.vim_mode_enabled`, default false) that gates whether Vim keybindings are active, plus a `vim_mode_enabled()` accessor consumed by the keymap layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Settings are declared via the `define_settings_group!` macro; each entry carries a toml_path, cloud-sync policy, and default, which the tree-sitter pass surfaces only as enum/accessor symbols.

nodes.name: vim_mode_enabled
nodes.summary: Accessor returning whether Vim mode is enabled by reading the `vim_mode` setting value; this boolean is the master gate that decides whether Vim keybindings and modal editing apply.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: User-config model (`WarpConfig`) and config-directory path resolution for the Warp-managed config files (themes, workflows, launch configs, tab configs). Its doc comment lists `keybindings.yaml` among the managed files, but the module exposes no dedicated keybindings path accessor or loader.

nodes.name: base_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the base data directory under which all user config lives (delegates to `warp_core::paths::data_dir`); this is the directory that also houses `keybindings.yaml`, though no helper here builds that specific path.

nodes.name: native.rs
nodes.summary: Native-platform user-config loader and filesystem watcher backing `WarpConfig`: subscribes to `WarpManagedPathsWatcher` and reloads themes, workflows, launch configs, tab configs, and settings on change. Notably, its change handler has no branch for `keybindings.yaml`, so edits to the keybindings file are not live-watched here.

nodes.name: handle_warp_managed_paths_event
nodes.summary: Filesystem-change handler that, per touched directory, reloads themes, workflows, launch configs (and tab configs / settings behind feature flags) and emits the matching update events. It dispatches only on themes/workflows/launch/tab-config dirs and the settings toml path — there is deliberately NO `keybindings.yaml` branch, so the watcher never reloads keybindings on edit.
nodes.languageNotes: Each branch spawns an async load via `ctx.spawn` and folds the result back into the model in the completion closure; the absence of a keybindings branch is the load-bearing detail for the keybindings subsystem.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root / barrel for the `vim` crate, declaring and re-exporting the Vim buffer-algorithm modules: matching-bracket finding, paragraph iteration, word iteration, find-char, text objects, the register store, and the `vim` state machine.

nodes.name: matching_brackets_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for `vim_find_matching_bracket`, sweeping cursor positions across a buffer of nested brackets and asserting the matched-bracket offset for the Vim `%` motion.

nodes.name: paragraph_iterator_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the paragraph iterator's `find_previous_paragraph_start` / `find_next_paragraph_end`, covering single paragraphs, surrounded paragraphs, first/last-paragraph boundaries, and cursors sitting inside runs of blank lines.

nodes.name: paragraph_iterator.rs
nodes.summary: Low-level paragraph-boundary scanner over a buffer, providing `find_previous_paragraph_start` and `find_next_paragraph_end` used by the Vim `{` / `}` motions and paragraph text objects.

nodes.name: find_previous_paragraph_start
nodes.summary: Scans backward from an offset over the buffer to locate the start of the previous paragraph (the boundary before a blank-line run), returning the offset or None at the buffer start.

nodes.name: find_next_paragraph_end
nodes.summary: Scans forward from an offset over the buffer to locate the end of the next paragraph (the boundary at the following blank-line run), returning the offset or None at the buffer end.

nodes.name: block_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the Vim `ab` (a-block) and `ib` (inner-block) bracket text objects, asserting selection spans for cursor positions inside and around a nested, indented block fixture.

nodes.name: paragraph_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Extensive unit tests for the `vim_inner_paragraph` (ip) and `vim_a_paragraph` (ap) text objects across empty buffers, single/two/three-paragraph layouts, blank-line runs, trailing blanks, and lines containing only spaces.

nodes.name: paragraph.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Vim paragraph text objects `vim_inner_paragraph` (ip) and `vim_a_paragraph` (ap), computing the selected span from a cursor offset using the paragraph-iterator boundaries plus blank-line inclusion rules.

nodes.name: vim_inner_paragraph
nodes.summary: Computes the `ip` (inner paragraph) selection span for a cursor offset: on a blank line it selects the consecutive blank run, otherwise the paragraph's content bounded by the previous start and next end.

nodes.name: vim_a_paragraph
nodes.summary: Computes the `ap` (a-paragraph) selection span, extending inner-paragraph bounds to also include the adjacent run of blank lines (trailing where present, otherwise leading) to match Vim's a-paragraph semantics.

nodes.name: word_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Comprehensive unit tests for the Vim word text objects — `iw`/`aw` (word) and `iW`/`aW` (BIGWORD) — verifying selection spans over mixed alphanumeric, symbol, and whitespace fixtures at many cursor positions.

nodes.name: word_iterator_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Exhaustive unit tests for `vim_word_iterator_from_offset` across forward/backward directions, Start/End word bounds, and Default vs BigWord types — covering the Vim `w`/`b`/`e`/`ge` motions and out-of-bounds error handling.

nodes.name: action.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the `Action` trait (the dispatchable, downcastable unit a keybinding maps to) with a blanket impl over any `Any + Debug + Send + Sync` type, plus the `ActionType` TypeId wrapper used to key actions in the keymap dispatch tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `std::any::Any`/`TypeId` to identify action types at runtime, working around the lack of stable trait upcasting via an explicit `as_any` method.

nodes.name: Action
nodes.summary: Trait representing a typed, dispatchable action that a keybinding triggers; requires `Any + Debug + Send + Sync` and exposes `as_any` (for downcasting in handlers) and a `type_name` default method.

nodes.name: ActionType
nodes.summary: Hashable newtype over `TypeId` identifying an action's concrete type, built via `ActionType::of::<T>()` or `From<&dyn Action>`, used as the map key that associates keybindings with action handlers.

nodes.name: context_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit test for `ContextPredicate::eval`, building a `Context` with set membership and key/value map entries and asserting identifier, equality, and combined predicates evaluate correctly.

nodes.name: context.rs
nodes.summary: Core keybinding context model: `Context` (a set of active identifiers plus a key→value map) and the `ContextPredicate` AST (Identifier/Equal/NotEqual/Not/And/Or/Just) with an `eval` evaluator, plus the `id!`/`eq!`/`ne!`/`always!` macros and operator overloads (`!`, `&`, `|`) used to author when-clauses.
nodes.languageNotes: Predicate construction is sugared via exported macros and `Not`/`BitAnd`/`BitOr` operator impls; `eval` resolves an absent map key as false for `Equal` but true for `NotEqual` (`unwrap_or(true)`), an asymmetry the overlap oracle must reproduce.

nodes.name: Context
nodes.summary: The keybinding evaluation context: a `HashSet` of active identifier flags and a `HashMap` of key→value entries against which `ContextPredicate`s are tested; `extend` merges another context's set and map in.

nodes.name: ContextPredicate
nodes.summary: Enum AST for keybinding when-clauses with variants Identifier, Equal, NotEqual, Not, And, Or, and Just(bool); these are the leaves and combinators that decide whether a binding is active in a given `Context`.

nodes.name: eval
nodes.summary: Recursively evaluates a `ContextPredicate` against a `Context`, resolving identifier membership and map key/value comparisons; an absent map key yields false for Equal and true for NotEqual. This is the oracle the keymap matcher and the overlap conflict checker both rely on.

nodes.name: overlap.rs
nodes.summary: Sound + complete predicate-overlap oracle for the keymap conflict model: `can_both_be_true` decides whether two `ContextPredicate`s can be simultaneously satisfied via bounded atom enumeration (no SAT crate, no unsafe), reusing `ContextPredicate::eval` as the per-assignment oracle so two bindings on the same keystroke only conflict when their when-clauses can co-occur.
nodes.languageNotes: Models Identifier leaves as independent booleans and Equal/NotEqual leaves per-key (one value per key plus an absent sentinel) to capture map-key exclusivity and the NotEqual absent-true asymmetry; an MAX_ATOMS/MAX_ASSIGNMENTS guard conservatively returns true and bumps an overflow counter that the walk harness asserts stays zero.

nodes.name: can_both_be_true
nodes.summary: Determines whether two `ContextPredicate`s are simultaneously satisfiable by collecting their atoms, enumerating every assignment of identifier booleans and per-key values (including an absent sentinel), and testing both predicates with `eval`; returns conservative `true` if the atom/assignment guard trips.

nodes.name: AtomSet
nodes.summary: Accumulator of a predicate's distinct atoms — identifier `ids` and per-key `map_values` — built by `collect`/`add`, merged via `union_with`, and sized by `atom_count`; it bounds the assignment space that `can_both_be_true` enumerates.

layers.name: Keymap Engine Core
layers.description: The compiled-in keybinding data model and matcher: Keymap (FixedBinding/EditableBinding/Trigger/Keystroke), the linear first-match-wins Matcher, ContextPredicate scoping, the sound+complete predicate-overlap conflict oracle, and the StandardAction/Action primitives.

layers.name: Dispatch & Responder Chain
layers.description: The runtime that turns a physical keystroke into an action: dispatch_keystroke -> Matcher.push_keystroke, the (ActionType,ViewType) action-handler registry, keymap_context construction, and the context merge up the responder chain.

layers.name: Modal Engine — Vim FSA
layers.description: The pure, buffer-agnostic vim keystroke interpreter (VimFSA -> VimEvent) plus the reusable, generic buffer algorithms (text objects, word/paragraph iterators, matching brackets, find-char) that any modal scheme could reuse.

layers.name: Modal Integration
layers.description: Where vim meets the editors: the printable-char input forks (vim_mode.is_some()), the dual id!("Vim")/!id!("Vim") binding registration, the "Vim"/"VimNormalMode" keymap context flags, and the TWO VimHandler implementations (code editor + terminal editor) that mutate buffers.

layers.name: Config & Persistence
layers.description: The keybindings.yaml user file (read/write/load/override-by-name), config path resolution, the config watcher (which notably has NO keybindings branch — external edits need a restart), and the vim_mode_enabled setting.

layers.name: Settings UI & Catalog
layers.description: The user-facing surfaces: the Keyboard-shortcuts editor (list/capture/ConflictMap/save), the CommandBinding bridge between the live keymap and the UI (live-apply + persist), and the read-only cheatsheet + static catalog.

layers.name: Binding Registration (Consumers)
layers.description: Representative call sites that register bindings into the keymap at view-init time — the root responder and the terminal view — illustrating the ~265 imperative register_*_bindings sites scattered across the app.

layers.name: Tests & Golden Snapshots
layers.description: The verification harness: matcher/context/overlap unit tests, the vim buffer-algorithm test suites, the keymap resolution golden-snapshot freeze that guards engine refactors, and the keyboard-protocol integration test.

tour.title: The Keymap: bindings as code
tour.description: Start at the heart. A single Keymap holds two parallel binding kinds — immutable FixedBinding and overridable EditableBinding — over a Trigger (Keystrokes/Standard/Custom/Empty) and a Keystroke. Note the new LayerStore: precedence is evolving beyond the old fixed-vs-editable LIFO.

tour.title: Matching: linear, first-match-wins
tour.description: The Matcher buffers pending keystrokes per view and linearly scans the keymap, returning the first binding whose keystrokes prefix-match and whose context predicate holds. A complete short binding shadows any longer chord sharing its prefix — there is no trie or ambiguity timeout.

tour.title: Context scoping & the conflict oracle
tour.description: ContextPredicate (id!/eq!/ne!/and/or/not) decides whether a binding is active. overlap.rs is the sound+complete oracle: can_both_be_true reuses ContextPredicate::eval to decide if two bindings on the same keystroke can EVER both be active — the principled answer to "is this a real conflict?".

tour.title: Dispatch: keystroke → action
tour.description: dispatch_keystroke builds the context from the responder chain (keymap_context), calls Matcher.push_keystroke, and routes the matched action through the (ActionType,ViewType) handler registry. This is the non-printable-key path.

tour.title: The user file: keybindings.yaml
tour.description: Customization lives in a flat keybindings.yaml (action-name -> keystroke; "none" = unbind). load_custom_keybindings runs once at launch, reading the file and applying each entry via set_custom_trigger. The schema cannot express context, platform, or Standard/Custom triggers.

tour.title: Override + persist, and the watcher gap
tour.description: set_custom_keybinding does BOTH: applies live via set_custom_trigger (no restart) AND persists via write_custom_keybinding. But the config watcher in native.rs has no keybindings.yaml branch — so EXTERNAL hand-edits still need a restart even though in-app edits apply instantly.

tour.title: Settings UI: list, capture, conflict
tour.description: The Keyboard-shortcuts editor lists ctx.editable_bindings() (unfiltered), captures a single keystroke (chords can't be captured yet), and flags conflicts via a ConflictMap keyed on bare Keystroke — context-blind, non-blocking, and not yet wired to the overlap.rs oracle.

tour.title: Modal engine: the pure FSA
tour.description: VimFSA is a pure keystroke→VimEvent interpreter that never touches a buffer. typed_character/keypress consume one key and return Option<VimEvent>; the verb-then-motion grammar lives here as hardcoded match arms. VimModel wraps it as an entity and emits events.

tour.title: Reusable buffer algorithms
tour.description: The buffer algorithms are generic over T: TextBuffer and reference no FSA/keymap state — text objects, word/paragraph iterators, bracket matching. This is the layer a Helix or Kakoune mode could reuse wholesale.

tour.title: Event → handler: the dispatch seam
tour.description: A blanket impl<T: VimHandler> VimSubscriber lowers each VimEvent to a VimHandler trait method via handle_vim_event. VimHandler is implemented TWICE — by CodeEditorView (here) and the terminal EditorView — which is where selection + buffer mutation actually happens.

tour.title: The printable-char input fork
tour.description: Printable chars never reach the matcher. handle_typed_characters forks on vim_mode.is_some() — vim_user_typed vs user_typed — via the RichTextAction factories. Non-char vim keys instead use DUAL binding registration with id!("Vim")/!id!("Vim") predicates (Enter vs VimEnter).

tour.title: Where bindings get registered
tour.description: Defaults are not a data table — they are registered imperatively at view-init across ~265 call sites. The root view and terminal view show the pattern: register_fixed_bindings / register_editable_bindings into the live keymap.

tour.title: The regression net: golden snapshots
tour.description: Finish at the safety harness. The resolution-snapshot test freezes (context, trigger, OS) -> winning action through the REAL matcher, so engine refactors that reorder bindings() can be diffed; the keyboard-protocol integration test exercises keystroke dispatch end-to-end.
